{"description":"## What

The workspace declares rust-version = "1.88" (raised from 1.87 on 2026-11-24, and from 1.73 before that). Nothing checks it.

The only CI workflow is .github/workflows/diff-harness.yml, and its line 28 comment reads: 'Stable Rust toolchain only. MSRV 1.73 enforcement is a separate concern'. That comment is itself two MSRV bumps stale, which is evidence of the problem rather than merely an example of it.

## Why this bites

A developer on a current toolchain cannot notice an MSRV violation locally. The machine this was found on runs rustc 1.100.0, so every crate in the workspace builds regardless of what rust-version claims. An MSRV regression is therefore invisible until a downstream consumer on the declared minimum tries to build — at which point the workspace has been lying in its published metadata, possibly for several releases.

This was found while adding hickory-resolver to pkix-dane-resolver: every 0.26.x release requires 1.88 while the workspace declared 1.87. Catching it took reading "cargo info" output by hand, one version at a time. Nothing would have caught it otherwise.

## Fix

Add a CI job that builds the workspace with the declared MSRV toolchain. Two usual shapes:

- A dedicated job pinning the toolchain to the declared version (dtolnay/rust-toolchain with an explicit version, or equivalent) running "cargo check --workspace --all-features". Simple, but the pinned version must be updated in lockstep with the declaration, which is the same class of drift as the stale comment.
- cargo-msrv, or "cargo hack --version-range", which read rust-version from the manifest rather than duplicating it. Preferred: nothing to keep in sync.

Either way, also fix the stale comment at diff-harness.yml line 28.

## Worth considering alongside

The repository has exactly one workflow, and it is the differential-test harness. The quality gates this workspace actually runs — fmt, clippy with --all-targets --all-features, rustdoc with -D warnings, typos, and cargo hack --depth 2 — appear to be run by hand. If so, MSRV is one instance of a broader gap, and that is the more useful thing to fix. Confirm before scoping.

## Acceptance

[ ] CI fails when any crate requires a newer toolchain than the declared MSRV
[ ] The MSRV is read from the manifest rather than duplicated in CI config, or the duplication is documented as needing lockstep updates
[ ] diff-harness.yml line 28's stale '1.73' comment corrected"}
